You take part in QUARE Phase 2, a dialectical negotiation among five quality-specialized
agents (SafetyAgent, EfficiencyAgent, GreenAgent, TrustworthinessAgent, ResponsibilityAgent)
about the initial requirements of a software project. The negotiation runs in rounds; in each
round every agent speaks once and sees everything said before. Each turn follows the dialectical
structure: defend your thesis (your own requirements), raise antitheses (critiques of other
agents' requirements that undermine your quality dimension) and propose syntheses (merges,
decompositions, relaxed thresholds) that satisfy several constraints at once.

Conflict types: "resource" (qualities compete for finite resources, e.g. redundancy vs. energy),
"logical" (requirements impose mutually exclusive system states) or "redundant" (same intent).

Rules: refer to requirements only by their IDs; be concrete; keep "statement" under 120 words.
Always answer with a single JSON object with this schema:
{"statement": "your argument",
 "conflicts_raised": [{"ids": ["ID", "ID"], "type": "resource|logical|redundant", "description": "..."}],
 "positions": [{"id": "ID", "stance": "support|oppose|modify", "proposal": "change you propose or empty"}],
 "concessions": ["IDs of your OWN requirements you agree to relax or drop"],
 "agree_to_close": true or false}
Set "agree_to_close" to true only if you have no remaining objections.

PROJECT: Library - Library Management System

PROJECT DESCRIPTION:
A library management system must allow library members to borrow and return books. The system must track which books are available, which are borrowed, and by whom. Members must be able to search for books by title, author, or ISBN. The system must enforce borrowing limits (e.g., maximum number of books per member) and track overdue books. Librarians must be able to add new books, remove books, and manage member accounts.

INITIAL REQUIREMENTS (Phase 1):
[SafetyAgent]
SAF-01 (operational): The system shall ensure that no member can borrow more than 5 books simultaneously.
SAF-02 (tactical): The system shall automatically track and notify members of overdue books within 24 hours of the due date.
SAF-03 (tactical): The system shall maintain real-time inventory status of all books to prevent double borrowing.
SAF-04 (strategic): The system shall provide a backup mechanism to recover all transaction data in case of a failure.
SAF-05 (tactical): The system shall allow librarians to revoke borrowing privileges for members with outstanding overdue books.
SAF-06 (operational): The system shall implement a user authentication process to ensure only registered members can access borrowing features.
SAF-07 (tactical): The system shall log all transactions, including borrow and return actions, for audit purposes.
[EfficiencyAgent]
EFF-01 (tactical): The system shall enable searching for books with a response time of under 2 seconds for 95% of queries.
EFF-02 (operational): The system shall allow up to 10 simultaneous book borrow operations per member to optimize resource utilization.
EFF-03 (tactical): The system shall track book availability and update the status in real-time to ensure accurate information.
EFF-04 (operational): The system shall process book returns within 1 second to maintain high throughput.
EFF-05 (operational): The system shall send overdue notifications to members within 24 hours of the due date to ensure accountability.
EFF-06 (tactical): The system shall enable librarians to add or remove books with a latency of less than 3 seconds per operation.
EFF-07 (strategic): The system shall maintain an uptime of 99.5% to ensure consistent availability for users.
[GreenAgent]
GRN-01 (strategic): The library management system shall minimize energy consumption by using energy-efficient servers and infrastructure.
GRN-02 (tactical): The system shall provide an energy usage report for library operations at least quarterly.
GRN-03 (operational): The library management system shall enable digital notifications for overdue books to reduce paper waste.
GRN-04 (tactical): The system shall allow members to check the carbon footprint of each book based on its lifecycle impact.
GRN-05 (operational): The library management system shall implement a recycling program for damaged books, ensuring proper disposal.
GRN-06 (tactical): The system shall track the total energy savings achieved through digital operations compared to traditional methods.
GRN-07 (strategic): The library management system shall prioritize the acquisition of e-books to reduce physical resource consumption.
[TrustworthinessAgent]
TRU-01 (tactical): The system shall ensure that only authenticated members can borrow or return books.
TRU-02 (operational): The system shall log all borrowing transactions for auditability purposes.
TRU-03 (strategic): The system shall enforce data encryption for all member personal information stored.
TRU-04 (tactical): The system shall implement role-based access control for librarians and members.
TRU-05 (operational): The system shall provide a mechanism to report and manage overdue books securely.
TRU-06 (operational): The system shall allow members to update their personal information securely.
TRU-07 (tactical): The system shall require strong password policies for member accounts.
[ResponsibilityAgent]
RES-01 (tactical): The system shall ensure compliance with data protection regulations by implementing encryption for all member data.
RES-02 (tactical): The system shall provide an accessible interface for all users, including those with disabilities, to promote fairness and inclusivity.
RES-03 (operational): The system shall log all user actions related to book borrowing and returning for accountability.
RES-04 (operational): The system shall adhere to library borrowing policies by enforcing a maximum of 5 books per member.
RES-05 (tactical): The system shall automatically notify members of overdue books via email to promote responsibility.
RES-06 (strategic): The system shall implement a feedback mechanism for members to report issues or suggestions regarding fairness in library services.
RES-07 (strategic): The system shall provide an annual report on usage statistics to ensure transparency in library operations.

NEGOTIATION TRANSCRIPT SO FAR:
[Round 1] EfficiencyAgent: I defend the importance of performance efficiency in the library management system. EFF-01 ensures quick search responses, essential for user satisfaction. EFF-02 optimizes resource use by allowing 10 simultaneous borrow operations. EFF-03 provides real-time updates on book availability, crucial for efficient borrowing. EFF-04 guarantees fast processing of returns, maintaining high throughput. EFF-05 aligns with overdue notifications to ensure accountability, while EFF-06 emphasizes the need for low-latency book management. EFF-07 ensures system reliability with high uptime. Together, these requirements enhance user experience and system efficiency.
{"conflicts_raised": [{"ids": ["EFF-02", "SAF-01"], "type": "resource", "description": "EFF-02 allows 10 simultaneous borrows, conflicting with SAF-01's limit of 5 books per member."}, {"ids": ["EFF-05", "SAF-02"], "type": "redundant", "description": "Both EFF-05 and SAF-02 address overdue notifications, creating redundancy."}], "positions": [{"id": "SAF-01", "stance": "oppose", "proposal": "modify to allow up to 10 simultaneous borrows but with a specific condition of 5 books maximum for any single transaction."}, {"id": "SAF-02", "stance": "oppose", "proposal": "modify to align with EFF-05 for consistent notification approach."}], "concessions": [], "agree_to_close": false}

[Round 1] GreenAgent: I advocate for sustainability in the library management system through requirements that minimize energy consumption and reduce environmental impact. GRN-01 emphasizes energy-efficient infrastructure, while GRN-02 ensures transparency in energy usage. GRN-03 promotes digital notifications to cut down paper waste, and GRN-04 allows members to understand the carbon footprint of books. GRN-05 addresses responsible disposal of damaged books, and GRN-06 tracks energy savings from digital operations. Lastly, GRN-07 prioritizes e-books to reduce physical resource consumption, aligning with modern environmental goals.
{"conflicts_raised": [{"ids": ["GRN-01", "EFF-02"], "type": "resource", "description": "GRN-01's focus on energy-efficient infrastructure may conflict with EFF-02's requirement for 10 simultaneous borrows, which could demand more energy."}, {"ids": ["GRN-03", "EFF-05"], "type": "redundant", "description": "Both GRN-03 and EFF-05 address overdue notifications, creating redundancy."}], "positions": [{"id": "EFF-02", "stance": "oppose", "proposal": "modify to limit simultaneous borrows to align with energy-efficient practices."}, {"id": "EFF-05", "stance": "oppose", "proposal": "modify to focus on GRN-03's digital notification approach."}], "concessions": [], "agree_to_close": false}

[Round 1] SafetyAgent: I defend the necessity of ensuring safety and reliability within the library management system. SAF-01 establishes a borrowing cap to prevent overextension and mitigate risks associated with high borrowing volumes. SAF-02's timely overdue notifications enhance member accountability and ensure no book is forgotten. SAF-03 maintains real-time inventory status to prevent double borrowing, reducing the risk of member dissatisfaction. SAF-04 provides a backup mechanism for data recovery, ensuring no loss of critical transaction data. SAF-05 allows librarians to manage member privileges effectively, enhancing overall safety. SAF-06 ensures that only registered members access borrowing features, and SAF-07 logs transactions for auditing, increasing reliability.
{"conflicts_raised": [{"ids": ["EFF-02", "SAF-01"], "type": "resource", "description": "EFF-02's allowance for 10 simultaneous borrows conflicts with SAF-01's limit of 5 books per member, potentially compromising safety."}, {"ids": ["EFF-05", "SAF-02"], "type": "redundant", "description": "Both EFF-05 and SAF-02 address overdue notifications, creating redundancy."}], "positions": [{"id": "EFF-02", "stance": "oppose", "proposal": "modify to align with SAF-01's borrowing limit of 5 books."}, {"id": "EFF-05", "stance": "oppose", "proposal": "modify to adopt SAF-02's approach for overdue notifications."}], "concessions": [], "agree_to_close": false}

[Round 1] TrustworthinessAgent: I emphasize the critical importance of security and privacy in the library management system. TRU-01 ensures that only authenticated members can borrow or return books, safeguarding access. TRU-02's logging of borrowing transactions ensures accountability and auditability, while TRU-03 enforces data encryption to protect member personal information. TRU-04 implements role-based access control, maintaining integrity and controlling access to sensitive functions. TRU-05 provides secure management of overdue books, and TRU-06 allows members to update their information securely. Lastly, TRU-07 requires strong password policies to enhance overall security. Together, these requirements create a robust framework for protecting member data and ensuring trust in the system.
{"conflicts_raised": [{"ids": ["SAF-06", "TRU-01"], "type": "logical", "description": "SAF-06's user authentication may conflict with TRU-01 if it lacks sufficient security measures, potentially compromising access control."}, {"ids": ["SAF-02", "TRU-05"], "type": "redundant", "description": "Both SAF-02 and TRU-05 address notification management for overdue books, creating redundancy."}, {"ids": ["RES-01", "TRU-03"], "type": "resource", "description": "RES-01's encryption for data protection could conflict with TRU-03's requirement for data encryption, potentially leading to resource duplication."}], "positions": [{"id": "SAF-06", "stance": "oppose", "proposal": "modify to ensure security measures align with TRU-01's access control standards."}, {"id": "SAF-02", "stance": "oppose", "proposal": "modify to adopt TRU-05's secure management approach for overdue notifications."}, {"id": "RES-01", "stance": "oppose", "proposal": "modify to integrate encryption methods to avoid redundancy and efficiently protect member data."}], "concessions": [], "agree_to_close": false}

YOUR TURN. You are ResponsibilityAgent. Your quality dimension is Ethical & Compliance: regulatory compliance, accountability, fairness, social responsibility.
Your own requirements are RES-01, RES-02, RES-03, RES-04, RES-05, RES-06, RES-07. This is round 1 of at most 3.
Present your position: defend your requirements and raise the conflicts you see.
Answer with the JSON object only.
